item.content:encoded:
Picasso vision "works" for a set object, like a person.
But what does 639 see when he looks at the wall of his cell? All angles of the wall, or all angles of the whole room it is attached to, or all angles of the whole building it is part of?

It's also unclear if he only seems to be facing in all directions at once in an onlookers perception; or is actually, physically occupying all possible orientations in one space. If the later, combined with the effect on his own vision, he would be seeing all angles of everything in all directions simultaneously. That is omnivision so useless that I think you would quickly adapt to behave as if blind.

They could probably get more useful interviews out of him in a room with no lights. Could be a good long-term therapy solution too.

To solve the less-than-useful-pointing dilemma. "Please take three steps in the direction you are currently facing."

-1 for fridge-logic fail. Although the root concept has serious potential.

item.content:encoded:
Has anyone here ever read "Flatland"? In that story, an entity in a two-dimensional space can see all of an entity in a one-dimensional space, and an entity in a three-dimensional space can see all of an entity in a two-dimensional space. When I read that, I theorized what a four-dimensional space would look like, based on that concept: In a four-dimensional space, you would be able to see all of an entity in a three-dimensional space.

And then, all these years later, I read this.

Spooky. +1

item.content:encoded:
Hrm, this one is….interesting. Definitely a neat concept, but it needs a lot of work in my opinion.

First off, your first interview log doesn't add very much, while the second adds nothing at all. Interview logs are meant to be used to demonstrate details that cannot be adequately conveyed through the standard report format. Your second one just repeats exactly what the report says, almost word for word. You also need to fix the format of the interview logs, they are kind of awkward.

But yeah, besides all that, I feel like this SCP just needs some oomph to it. Right now it's just "okay, he looks funny. So?" It needs some kind of hook, or catch, something to make it work. Take 682 for example: on it's own, an unkillable lizard just isn't that interesting. Add in a desire to massacre humanity, and you have something worth fearing. That being said, don't make this one "just kills everything" or "makes you go crazy", those have been overdone.

Withholding vote pending an update or lack thereof.

So yeah, there's my two cents. Good luck!

EDIT: Just saw that you fixed the interview log format. Well done.
